newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end mixed amid heating oil losses.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end mixed amid heating oil losses.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices ended mixed Thursday as traders sold heating oil to buy gasoline and crude amid slackening distillate demand in the U.S. Gulf cash market.

"There was tremendous selling in the heat crack and selling of heat to buy gasoline as very tight heat supplies in the (U.S.) Gulf significantly relaxed," said Nauman Barakat, trader with Prudential Securities in New York.
March heating oil settled 0.93 cent lower at 59.92 cents a gallon. The March heating oil-to-crude crack spread fell to $3.11 a barrel from $3.70 a barrel Wednesday.
Nearby heat was deemed technically weak after breaching 59.55 cents, which had been March's low for the week, and falling to 59.45 cents.
Chartists pegged support at 58.75 cents, the beginning of a price gap for March heat made September 3 that extends to 58.05 cents.
Crude was bought as the heat crack was sold, leaving prompt crude's price at a healthy technical level by the close, dealers said.
March crude ended at $22.02, up 16 cents a barrel while March gasoline finished up 0.29 cent a gallon at 63.18 cents.

"I think it's significant that crude is able to close around $22.00. On a chart basis, it's good support," said Jeff Foose, trader with KCS Energy in New Jersey. March crude set a shelf of support between $22.00 and $22.25 late last September.
A spate of refinery maintenance and shipping deadlines had tightened spot distillate supplies in the U.S. Gulf early this week, firming cash prices there and widening the March/April heat spread.
But, by Thursday refineries began to announce their return from seasonal turnaround, and the shipping deadlines had passed.
Lyondell-Citgo, in particular, started up a $1.1 billion upgrade at its Houston refinery Wednesday with the plant running near design capacity of 235,000 barrels a day.
The March/April heat spread closed at 1.82 cents after widening from 1.88 cents Monday to 2.13 cents on Wednesday.

Demand was for heating oil was only seen detriorating with the National Weather Service's six to 10 day forecast starting February 18 calling for seasonally warm temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, which has the largest concentration of heating oil users in the world.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
